transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... it's probably nothing too serious, but I've been making a few, um, just kind of silly mistakes at work lately. 

I supervise a sales team, and I just keep messing up on our sales reports. Like, just copying the wrong numbers over from the team dashboard, or maybe missing a line in a procedure I was supposed to check off. And the thing is, I swear I thought I went over it, you know? 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I really do try to be thorough and do a good job for my team. I hope I'm explaining this right... is that the sort of thing you usually help people with?
Roughly how long have you been experiencing these kinds of mistakes and attention issues?

Um, well, I guess it really started becoming more of an issue... or, well, I started noticing it more since I got promoted. I moved into this supervisor role about a year and two months ago. 

Before that, I was just on the floor selling, and I always did really well with that. But since taking on the team, it's just been a bit of an adjustment with all the extra paperwork and reports. So, yeah, about a year and a couple of months. I mean, it's not like I'm doing a terrible job overall, I promise, it's just these little slip-ups here and there. 

Does that make sense? Is it normal for things like this to pop up after a promotion?
Looking back to when you were in school or growing up, did you ever struggle with focus, organization, or careless mistakes back then?

Um, well... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, yeah, I kind of was. It's a little embarrassing to admit, but my mom actually still jokes about it. She kept some of my old teacher notes from elementary school. 

I think I was just a really energetic kid, you know? But the notes did say things like I rushed through my assignments a bit, or... or that I'd lose my homework sometimes. And, um, I guess I had a habit of talking out of turn, or needing to be reminded to stay in my seat. I was just really eager to participate, I think! 

I mean, a lot of little boys are like that, right? It wasn't anything malicious or terrible, I promise. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for?
As an adult now, do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have difficulty sitting still for extended periods?

Um, well... I guess I do get a little antsy sometimes. It's not like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything disruptive, I really try to be respectful of everyone's time. But, um, when I have to sit through those really long management meetings, it almost feels like... like my body is just sort of buzzing inside? 

I try to keep it under control, but I'll catch myself shifting around in my chair a lot, or maybe tapping my foot under the table where no one can see. Sometimes I just have to make a quick excuse to get up and grab some water or use the restroom, just to stretch my legs for a second. 

I think a lot of people probably get a little stiff sitting for that long, though, right? I hope it doesn't make me sound like I'm not paying attention, because I really do listen to what's being said. Is that kind of what you meant?
Do these difficulties with keeping organized, misplacing things, or staying on track happen at home or in your personal life as well?

Um, well... yeah, I suppose it does. It's... gosh, it's a little hard to admit, because I really do try my best to be there for everyone. But at home, it's been causing a little bit of conflict lately. People feel like they can't count on me to follow through on things I say I'll do. I always mean to, I promise! I just... things just slip my mind, or I get sidetracked. 

And, um... I guess I should probably tell you, since I want to be totally honest with you... it's actually gotten to the point at work where my manager put it in a formal review. I was so embarrassed when they brought it up, because I really do care about my job and my team. I'm working really hard to fix it and get back on track, though, I don't want you to think I'm just slacking off. 

I hope that's okay to share... is that the kind of thing you needed to know?
Do you find yourself frequently interrupting others or finishing their sentences before they can finish speaking?

Um, well... I guess I might do that sometimes. I really don't mean to be rude, I promise! It's just... in meetings, I get so enthusiastic, and I think I know exactly where the other person is going with their thought. So I'll just sort of jump in to agree or answer before they're totally finished. 

I'm just trying to be helpful and keep things moving, you know? But then, um, sometimes I realize I completely missed the mark and answered the wrong point, or I see that I cut somebody off when they had more to say. I always feel terrible when that happens and I try to apologize right away. I really value my team's input. 

I think maybe I just get a little too eager sometimes... I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad listener. Is that the sort of thing you're asking about?
